strengths: Ambitious scale and scope: SpatialVID compiles over 2.7 million video clips (~7,089 hours) of real-world dynamic scenes, alongside a curated high-quality subset (SpatialVID-HQ, ~1,146 hours), addressing a clear need for large-scale dynamic video data with 3D/camera information.

Comprehensive annotation suite: The dataset couples video frames with multi-modal annotations, including camera poses, metric/relative depth maps, dynamic object masks (via SAM 2), discrete motion instructions (keyboard-style cinematographic controls), and structured hierarchical captions.

Well-designed curation and refinement pipeline: The paper introduces thoughtful engineering solutions, such as conditioning large language models (LLM) on estimated camera poses to eliminate directional hallucinations in visual captions, as well as multi-criteria filtering (aesthetics, luminance, OCR, motion dynamics).

Thorough descriptive statistics: Section 4 provides clear statistical breakdowns and comparisons against existing datasets (e.g., Panda-70M), demonstrating improved motion diversity, trajectory turn distributions, and caption granularity.
weaknesses: Complete lack of downstream empirical evaluation: The paper does not train or evaluate any model using SpatialVID. There are no experiments showing whether pre-training or fine-tuning on SpatialVID improves performance on downstream tasks such as camera-controlled video generation (e.g., CameraCtrl, MotionCtrl), novel view synthesis, or feed-forward pose/depth estimation.

No quantitative evaluation of pseudo-ground-truth quality: All geometric annotations (camera trajectories, depth, and dynamic masks) are generated by automated models (MegaSaM, UniDepth v2, Depth Anything v2, SAM 2). Monocular dynamic SLAM and monocular depth predictors are known to suffer from drift, scale ambiguity, and tracking failures. The manuscript does not benchmark this annotation pipeline against real-world datasets with verified ground truth (e.g., TartanAir, ScanNet, Waymo, or PointOdyssey) to quantify trajectory and depth error rates.

Absence of human verification or evaluation for semantic annotations: The multi-stage structured captioning relies entirely on Gemini-2.0-flash and Qwen3-30B-A3B. While Figure 9 illustrates a positive qualitative case study, there is no quantitative human evaluation or user study assessing hallucination rates, spatial accuracy, or instruction faithfulness across the corpus.

strengths: Impressive scale and scope: SpatialVID compiles over 2.7 million video clips (7,089 hours), featuring a well-curated 1,146-hour high-quality subset (SpatialVID-HQ) capturing diverse real-world dynamic scenes.

Comprehensive multi-modal annotations: The dataset provides aligned per-frame camera poses, depth maps, dynamic masks, structured multi-aspect captions, and discretized motion instructions (e.g., WASD-style navigation controls).

Thoughtful curation pipeline: The procedural filtering (incorporating aesthetic scoring, luminance, OCR text density, motion intensity, and trajectory consistency checks) and the use of geometric priors to correct VLM caption hallucinations are well-designed.
weaknesses: Total absence of downstream empirical validation: The paper does not train or evaluate any downstream models (such as camera-controlled video generation, novel view synthesis, feedforward 3D reconstruction, or world modeling) using SpatialVID. Demonstrating that training on SpatialVID / SpatialVID-HQ improves performance over existing datasets (e.g., Panda-70M, RealEstate10K, or CamVid-30K) is essential to substantiate its real-world utility.

Lack of quantitative error benchmarking for pseudo-ground-truth annotations: All 3D geometric annotations (poses, depths, dynamic masks) are generated via automated algorithms (MegaSaM, Depth Anything v2, SAM2) rather than physical sensor measurements. The submission lacks a quantitative evaluation (e.g., on datasets with metric ground truth like TartanAir or ScanNet) assessing the pose drift, depth accuracy, and failure rate of the pipeline.

Data distribution and legal/ethical considerations: The dataset relies on scraping over 21,000 hours of YouTube videos. The paper does not discuss video licensing, copyright compliance, terms of service, or protocols for handling personally identifiable information (PII) and dataset maintenance/hosting.

strengths: Substantial data curation effort: Curating and processing over 21,000 hours of raw video into 2.7M dynamic clips (7,089 hours) annotated with camera poses, depth, dynamic masks, and structured captions is an impressive engineering achievement addressing a genuine data bottleneck.

Well-designed annotation pipeline: Upgrading MegaSaM with modern depth models (UniDepth v2, Depth Anything v2) and leveraging SAM2 for dynamic foreground masking addresses critical failure modes in monocular dynamic SLAM.

Pose-conditioned structured captioning: Grounding LLM/VLM video captioning with explicit geometric poses effectively mitigates directional hallucinations (e.g., distinguishing panning left vs. right) and provides actionable motion instructions.
weaknesses: Complete lack of downstream empirical evaluation: The paper does not conduct any model training, fine-tuning, or benchmarking experiments on downstream tasks (e.g., camera-controlled video generation, novel view synthesis, or 3D reconstruction). Consequently, the claim that the dataset 'directly foster[s] improved model generalization and performance' is entirely unsubstantiated by empirical machine learning results.

Absence of quantitative error analysis for pseudo-ground-truth annotations: All 3D annotations (camera trajectories, depth maps, dynamic masks) are generated by automated foundation models rather than physical sensors. There is no rigorous quantitative validation (e.g., measuring ATE/RPE on datasets with physical ground truth like TartanAir or Waymo) to assess the error rate, drift, or failure frequency of the pipeline.

Unaddressed dataset licensing, privacy, and distribution logistics: Scraping 33k+ YouTube videos raises significant concerns regarding copyright, privacy (e.g., identifiable faces and license plates in public outdoor/indoor tours), and dataset longevity. The paper does not specify how the video data and annotations will be legally and stably distributed to the community.
Minor editorial and presentation flaws: The manuscript contains multiple typos and grammatical oversights (e.g., 'dataaset' on page 3, 'processe' on page 8, and informal phrasing throughout).
